sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: earlier-letter network across thirteen comment letters on one SEC proposal (hook h1). Each commenter states its own earlier letters; one commenter's second letter is shown only by a different commenter. Target medium per the user's instruction of 2026-10-12 ("no slot for Easy Tier ... target medium and high"); the task page saved at 00:54 the same day reads "Medium questions are full on this set — only a Hard or Easy question can still be submitted" (Hard 0/2 · Medium 3/3 · Easy 0/1), reported to the user. Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 3 L14 (three dates) -> MFA in. Doc 13 L20 (two dates) -> Blockchain Association in. Doc 6 L16 and L26 (one letter, May 8, 2023) plus Doc 8 L89 and L99 (June 2023 letter, comment-file link s70423-206999-417002) with Doc 10 L207 (May 8 letter, link s70423-189019-370362) -> IAA has two -> in. Minimal inputs: Doc 3, Doc 13, Doc 8, and Doc 6 or Doc 10.
- Universe: thirteen commenters, earlier letters of their own as the letters show them. Three: MFA (May 8, July 24, September 12, 2023, the last one joint). Two: Blockchain Association (May 8 and October 27, 2023), IAA (May 8 and June 2023). One: Real Estate Roundtable (joint letter, Sep. 12, 2023, Doc 2 L18), FIA (May 8, 2023, Doc 9 L13), JPMorgan (May 8, 2023, Doc 10 L14 and L22), AICPA (8 May 2023, Doc 11 L14), AGC (March 8, 2023, Doc 12 L17). None: Blackstone (Doc 1; August 2 meeting only), ASA (Doc 4), TIAA and Nuveen (Doc 5), Milbank (Doc 7), ICAN (Doc 8 L38: comments it was "unable to provide during the prior open period"). Every dated reference to an earlier letter was listed by search ("May 8, 2023", "8 May 2023", "May 2023", "June", "July 24", "Sep. 12", "September 12", "March 8", "October 27", "Oct. 27", "Apr.") and read in place.
- Necessity: Doc 3 is the only place MFA's earlier letters are attributed to MFA (Docs 1 and 2 cite the joint letter without naming MFA). Doc 13 is the only source for the Blockchain Association's two dates. Doc 8 is the only source for the IAA's June letter ("June" elsewhere: Doc 10 L103, the LSTA's letter, and L230, a job title). The IAA's May 8 letter is printed in Doc 6 and in Doc 10, so the two are grouped as alternatives. Removal: without Doc 3 the answer loses MFA, without Doc 13 the Blockchain Association, without Doc 8 or without both Doc 6 and Doc 10 the IAA. No mandatory model removal probes.
- Selected-lever checks: which-items decoys that fail the test: AGC (one letter; the August 29, 2023 meeting and November 9, 2023 call are staff contacts), Real Estate Roundtable (one joint letter), FIA, JPMorgan and AICPA (one letter each, all dated May 8, 2023, the same date as the IAA's first), Blackstone (cites the joint letter and the AIC's letter, neither its own). Who belongs where: the IAA's second letter is named in ICAN's letter, not in the IAA's.
- Targeted failure modes: Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list: own-account reading gives "Managed Funds Association and Blockchain Association" (Doc 6 L16 and L26 show one IAA letter); recomputed from the universe above. Considered and not declared: counting the letter in the bundle as an earlier one (gives seven names; the wording says "earlier"); counting AGC's staff meeting and call as letters (gives four names; not a trap the form's list clearly covers).
- Calculation verification: not applicable beyond counting letters per commenter; counts recomputed from the quoted sentences on 2026-10-12 (3, 2, 2, then five ones and five zeros).
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no passage lists the three commenters. The capture's bundle overview prints for Doc 8 the dates "May 2023 · June 2023" without saying what they are, for Doc 3 "May 8, 2023 · July 24, 2023" and for Doc 13 "May 8, 2023 · October 27, 2023"; none states a count. Shortest complete route: Doc 3 L14, Doc 13 L20, Doc 6 L26, Doc 8 L89.
- Precision/readings: "more than one earlier comment letter" = two or more letters sent before the commenter's letter in this set. Narrow reading that sets aside MFA's joint and aggregate-cost letters: MFA itself lists all three as "comments we submitted" on the proposal. Loose reading of "commenters" that takes in cited third parties (AIC, LSTA, Mercatus Center, the four audit firms, ABA, SIFMA AMG): each has one cited letter, so the answer is unchanged. The bundle cannot show earlier letters that no letter mentions; the answer is the set the letters show.
- Completeness: no source gaps (capture: 13 of 13 documents read in full; intake hashes match). All thirteen letters were read in full for this candidate.
- Style/set review: 21 words, one ask, no document named, no answer part in the question. Sketches i02 and i05 share this answer path (earlier-letter network) and would be siblings; i04 is a different family.

sections.question: Which of these commenters, if any, had already sent the SEC more than one earlier comment letter on its safeguarding proposal?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 3, opening paragraph): the Managed Funds Association says its comments "supplement comments we submitted to the Commission on May 8, 2023", on July 24, 2023 and on September 12, 2023. That is three earlier letters, so it qualifies (component c1).
Step 2. Source input (Doc 13, third paragraph): the Blockchain Association "previously submitted comment letters in response to the Proposed Rule on May 8, 2023 and October 27, 2023". That is two earlier letters, so it qualifies (component c3).
Step 3. Source input (Doc 6, first page footnotes): the Investment Adviser Association (IAA) cites one earlier letter of its own, dated May 8, 2023, which it calls its Initial Safeguarding Letter. Read alone, the IAA has one earlier letter.
Step 4. Source input (Doc 8 and Doc 10, the passage on advisers made to enforce the rule and JPMorgan's footnote on internal controls): ICAN quotes "the Investment Adviser Association in their June 2023 letter" and links it in the SEC's comment file for this proposal. Doc 10 cites the IAA's May 8, 2023 letter under a different link in the same file. The June letter is therefore a second letter, not the May one.
Step 5. Count (Doc 6 and Doc 8, combining Steps 3 and 4): the IAA had sent two earlier letters, one in May and one in June 2023, so it qualifies (component c2).
Step 6. Exclusions, from the other commenters' own letters: the Real Estate Roundtable (a joint trade-association letter), the Futures Industry Association, JPMorgan, the AICPA and the Association of Global Custodians each cite one earlier letter of their own. The custodians' meeting and call with staff are not comment letters. Blackstone, the American Securities Association, TIAA and Nuveen, Milbank and ICAN cite no earlier letter of their own.
Decoy: the Investment Adviser Association looks like a one-letter commenter in its own submission, beside five others that really have one. Only ICAN's quotation shows its second letter.
Final answer (Doc 3, Doc 13, Doc 6 and Doc 8): Managed Funds Association, Investment Adviser Association and Blockchain Association.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 6 cites only the IAA's May 8, 2023 letter; its June 2023 letter appears only in Doc 8, where ICAN quotes it. Reading each commenter's own account gives Managed Funds Association and Blockchain Association; joining Docs 6 and 8 adds the Investment Adviser Association.
